data.ruling: The stock verifier's refutation stands on sourcing rule 4 (stock gate). JLCPCB's exact match for C2868250 has stockCount 1 and canPresaleNumber -94. The need is 5 boards (S7) x 2 placements (F1, IOBoard.md:427) = 10. The S4 threshold is max(5 x 10, 50) = 50. 1 < 50 fails the gate. A negative presale count fails rule 4 whatever the stock says. Rule 6 cannot stand in: the owner's personal-library export of 2026-09-25 lists no INA238 or any other INA2xx part. Digi-Key reads 0 in all three packagings, so the rule-5 second-vendor route fails too. The datasheet verifier's confirmation does not change this, because rule 4 is a sourcing gate. Scope is part. The S4 floor of 50 is above a stock of 1 at any placement count, and the negative presale count fails at every need. So the part fails rule 4 in every function, not only in this one. Lifecycle passes and is not a ground. TI's product page carries meta status ACTIVE and one marketingStatusDescription ACTIVE, with no NRND, last-time-buy or obsolete text. Digi-Key reads Active, with discontinued false and end_of_life false. The LCSC identity agrees: C2868250 is INA238AIDGSR from Texas Instruments in VSSOP-10. The INA238 is a fixed input (Research.md Scope, 'Motor monitor | INA238'). By Scope, a fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner and is not re-selected. This ruling goes to the owner. The rule-5 alternate the verifier names, INA237AIDGSR, was not re-read in this ruling.
